components: API tier for shorten and redirect, an ID generator using per-host counter ranges, a sharded metadata store keyed by code hash, a cache for hot URLs, and an offline analytics pipeline fed by a queue.
dataflow: Write path: POST /v1/shorten validates input, reserves a code from the host's range, writes the mapping, returns the code. Read path: GET /{code} checks the cache first; on a miss it reads the shard, populates the cache, and issues a 302. Click events go to the queue, never the redirect path.
requirements: Shorten URLs at 100M new URLs per month with a 10:1 read-to-write ratio. Must support custom aliases and link expiry. Redirects need p99 under 100ms.
scale: Reads shard cleanly by code hash. The ID generator is the write bottleneck: per-host ranges avoid coordination. Cache absorbs the 10:1 read ratio. Custom-alias contention is handled with a conditional write on the alias key.
tradeoffs: Chose per-host counter ranges over a key-generation service for simplicity, giving up globally ordered codes. Chose lazy expiry on read plus a sweeper over TTL-only deletes to avoid thundering deletes.
